newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: WORLD SOYBEAN DEMAND TO DROP IN Q3 -- OIL WORLD.
newsitem.headline: WORLD SOYBEAN DEMAND TO DROP IN Q3 -- OIL WORLD.

text.p: World soybean import needs are likely to decline betweeen July and September as processors, particularly in Europe, draw down large stockpiles built earlier in the year, Hamburg-based newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.
This should result in a sharp fall in U.S. soybean exports to 2.5 million tonnes between June and August 1997, against a 12-year high of 4.2 million registered in the same 1996 period.

"Many crushers stepped up purchases...in the past two months due to supply, weather and price uncertainties, as well as concern about possible Brazilian bottlenecks in the internal transportation system and export facilities," it said.

Brazilian beans in particular have been arriving in Europe in "huge quantities", it said, giving processors the breathing space to ride out the summer months. Between March and May period disposals of Brazilian, Argentine and U.S. beans increased more sharply than expected, and were up two million tonnes on the same period last year.

"Argentine and Brazilian farmers boosted their new-crop sales at an unprecendented rate, responding to the attractive prices, which gave them every incentive to market their crop before the new northern hemisphere supplies arrive."
"The huge Brazilian exports in April and May confirmed that the export facilities were expanded significantly during the past year," Oil World added.
Processors in Europe will run down their stocks in anticipation of the new bumper U.S. soybean harvest becoming available at attractive prices from the end of September onwards, it said.
